title: Check DL560's NUMA effect on many-thread runs, and try mimalloc as TermAl's global allocator
outcome: We know from measurements on one host whether NUMA and the allocator contribute to the stalls DL560 shows at high thread counts, and TermAl has a mimalloc change prepared with its effect, platform support and correctness stated, so Greg can decide on landing from numbers rather than from an assumption.
acceptance: DL560's NUMA topology is recorded, and a same-commit, same-filter comparison on DL560 alone separates NUMA placement from thread count without code changes: at least default threads, matched threads unbound, and one node bound with its local memory, each with test time, over-60 s count, failures and cross-node allocation figures

A candidate makes mimalloc the global allocator for the TermAl binary, with Cargo.lock and license policy satisfied, and builds on Linux, Windows and Mac with the toolchains those hosts already have; nothing is installed on any host to make it build

The same comparison and a representative long-running or product-shaped workload run with and without mimalloc on one host, reporting throughput or time, resident memory and any failures; the results say plainly if there is no benefit, and no cause is claimed that the numbers don't show

Correctness: the candidate passes a review pair and the full gate on the exact input, with memory growth over a long run and the release build path from the master checkout addressed; landing follows the standing rule only if the measurements support it, and Greg gets the numbers and the recommendation either way
